trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway - Free Theme Park Shuttle
hotel.location: 7470 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, US (28.3314,-81.5863)

day_by_day.morning: No activities - flight arrives late night
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities - flight arrives late night
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 22:30 via United Airlines. Collect luggage and take the Magical Express or a budget rideshare (Lyft/Uber ~$25-35) to Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway. Check in, unpack essentials, and review your Disney World park tickets and schedule for the week. Stop by the hotel vending machines or nearby 7-Eleven on W Irlo Bronson Hwy for late-night snacks.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport food before departure
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food
meals.dinner: Late-night snacks from hotel vending machine or 7-Eleven (~$5-10). Alternatively, grab a quick bite at McDonald's or Taco Bell on W Irlo Bronson Hwy, both open late and within 1 mile of the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Disney World tickets in advance online to save money — look for multi-day tickets which offer the best per-day value. Download the My Disney Experience app before arrival. Confirm the hotel's free theme park shuttle schedule at check-in. Get to bed early — big days ahead! Hotel address: 7470 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (6:30 AM) and grab the hotel's free theme park shuttle to Magic Kingdom — aim to arrive at rope drop (park opening, typically 9:00 AM). Head straight to Tomorrowland or Fantasyland to ride the most popular attractions before crowds build: Space Mountain, Seven Dwarfs Mine Train (use Lightning Lane if budget allows), and Peter Pan's Flight. Use the My Disney Experience app to monitor wait times and grab virtual queues if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, explore Liberty Square and Adventureland — ride Pirates of the Caribbean, The Haunted Mansion, and Big Thunder Mountain Railroad. Take a mid-afternoon break during peak heat (1–3 PM) by enjoying indoor attractions like the Walt Disney World Railroad or the Carousel of Progress. Watch the Festival of Fantasy Parade (check schedule in app) which typically runs in the early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the iconic Happily Ever After fireworks show (typically 9:00 PM) — find a spot on Main Street U.S.A. at least 45 minutes early for the best view. Ride any remaining must-do attractions during the evening when crowds thin. Take the hotel shuttle back after the fireworks.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel before departure or grab a quick continental breakfast if offered. Alternatively, stop at a Publix or Walmart on W Irlo Bronson Hwy the night before to pack sandwiches and snacks (~$8-12 per person) — Disney allows outside food!
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square — budget-friendly counter service with fish and chips, clam chowder, and chicken sandwiches (~$12-16 per person). One of Magic Kingdom's best value spots.
meals.dinner: Cosmic Ray's Starlight Café in Tomorrowland — large portions of burgers, chicken, and rotisserie options at counter-service prices (~$13-18 per person). Eat before the fireworks show.

day_by_day.notes: Pack a refillable water bottle — Disney has free water cup stations at all quick-service restaurants. Wear comfortable shoes and apply sunscreen. June in Orlando is hot and humid (highs ~90°F/32°C) with frequent afternoon thunderstorms — pack a small poncho. Arrive at the shuttle stop 15 minutes early.

day_by_day.morning: Take the hotel shuttle to EPCOT for rope drop. Head immediately to Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (virtual queue — join as soon as the park opens via the app) and Test Track. Explore Future World / World Discovery and World Nature sections early, including Soarin' Around the World and Living with the Land boat ride. The aquarium at The Seas with Nemo & Friends is a great free-feeling bonus attraction included with park admission.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon exploring the World Showcase — walk the 1.2-mile promenade around World Showcase Lagoon visiting pavilions representing 11 countries (Mexico, Norway, China, Germany, Italy, America, Japan, Morocco, France, United Kingdom, Canada). Each pavilion has free entertainment, cultural exhibits, and unique merchandise. Ride Frozen Ever After in the Norway Pavilion (expect waits — go early or use Lightning Lane). Watch the cultural performances scheduled throughout the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for EPCOT's spectacular nighttime show — EPCOT Forever or Luminous The Global Celebration (check current show schedule). Watch from the World Showcase Lagoon promenade. Grab a snack from one of the World Showcase kiosks before heading back on the hotel shuttle.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from the hotel or bring snacks from a grocery store. Alternatively, grab a quick bite at Sunshine Seasons in The Land pavilion — one of EPCOT's best value counter-service spots with fresh, healthy options (~$10-14).
meals.lunch: Sunshine Seasons in The Land pavilion — excellent value with rotating seasonal dishes, sandwiches, and Asian-inspired bowls (~$12-16 per person). Sit inside in the air conditioning!
meals.dinner: Katsura Grill in the Japan Pavilion — counter-service Japanese food including sushi, udon, and teriyaki at reasonable prices (~$14-18 per person). Eat before the nighttime show and find a good viewing spot.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is the most walkable park — comfortable shoes are essential. The World Showcase doesn't open until 11:00 AM, so plan Future World attractions for the morning. Many World Showcase pavilions offer free cultural entertainment and exhibits. Stay hydrated — free water cups are available at all quick-service locations.

day_by_day.morning: Take the hotel shuttle to Hollywood Studios for rope drop. This park requires the most strategic planning. Join the virtual queue for Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance the moment the park opens (via the My Disney Experience app) — this is one of Disney's most impressive rides. Head immediately to Slinky Dog Dash in Toy Story Land (very popular, long waits later). Ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run in Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge early.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, explore Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge more thoroughly — visit Dok-Ondar's Den of Antiquities and Oga's Cantina (reservations recommended but walk-ups sometimes available). Ride Tower of Terror and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster in Sunset Boulevard. Watch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular (check show times — typically multiple shows daily) — a free, impressive live stunt show included with park admission.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the Fantasmic! nighttime spectacular (check schedule — typically 8:00 or 9:00 PM). Arrive at the Hollywood Hills Amphitheater at least 30-45 minutes early for good seats. This is one of Disney's best free-included nighttime shows. Ride any remaining attractions during the evening rush when some queues shorten. Take the hotel shuttle back.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks or eat at the hotel before departure. Grab a quick coffee and pastry at Trolley Car Café on Hollywood Boulevard (~$6-9).
meals.lunch: Woody's Lunch Box in Toy Story Land — one of Hollywood Studios' most beloved counter-service spots with grilled cheese, BBQ brisket melts, and 'totchos' (~$12-15 per person). Expect a line but it moves quickly.
meals.dinner: ABC Commissary — large counter-service restaurant with burgers, wraps, and international-inspired dishes at reasonable prices (~$13-17 per person). Eat before Fantasmic! to secure good seats.

day_by_day.notes: Hollywood Studios is the most 'virtual queue heavy' park — have the My Disney Experience app ready at park opening. Lightning Lane purchases can be worth it here for Rise of the Resistance if virtual queue is unavailable. Bring ponchos — afternoon storms are common in June. The park can feel crowded in the afternoon; use the app to monitor wait times.

day_by_day.morning: Take the hotel shuttle to Animal Kingdom for rope drop. Head directly to Pandora – The World of Avatar: ride Avatar Flight of Passage (the park's most popular ride — expect long waits later) and Na'vi River Journey. The immersive Pandora land is stunning even outside the rides. Then head to Africa to ride Kilimanjaro Safaris early morning when animals are most active in the cooler temperatures.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, explore Asia — ride Expedition Everest (one of Disney's best roller coasters) and Kali River Rapids (you WILL get wet — great on a hot June day!). Watch the Festival of the Lion King show in Africa (check times — a spectacular Broadway-style performance included with admission). Explore the Maharajah Jungle Trek and Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail — free walking trails with incredible animal encounters.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the Rivers of Light nighttime show or Tree of Life Awakenings (check current schedule). Animal Kingdom typically closes earlier than other parks, so plan accordingly. Return to the hotel by shuttle by 8:00-9:00 PM. Spend the evening relaxing at the hotel pool, doing laundry, and recharging for the final days. Pick up groceries at a nearby Publix or Walmart for snacks.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks or eat at the hotel. Grab a Pongu Pongu drink and snack in Pandora (~$6-8) as a fun treat.
meals.lunch: Flame Tree Barbecue in Discovery Island — one of Animal Kingdom's best counter-service restaurants with smoked ribs, pulled pork, and chicken at great value (~$13-17 per person). Beautiful outdoor seating overlooking the water.
meals.dinner: Yak & Yeti Local Food Cafes (counter service) in Asia — Asian-inspired dishes including fried rice, noodles, and chicken bowls at budget-friendly prices (~$12-15 per person). Or head back to the hotel area and dine at one of the many affordable restaurants on W Irlo Bronson Hwy (Denny's, IHOP, or local spots).

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom is best experienced in the morning — animals are more active and temperatures are cooler. The park is very walkable and lush — enjoy the incredible theming and landscaping. Kali River Rapids will soak you — bring a change of clothes or wear quick-dry clothing. This is a great day to use as a 'lighter' park day since Animal Kingdom often closes earlier.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a relaxed morning at the hotel. Take a dip in the hotel pool. Walk or take a short rideshare to a nearby Publix Supermarket on W Irlo Bronson Hwy to stock up on affordable groceries, snacks, and drinks for the remaining days (~$20-30 for the group). This saves significant money compared to buying all meals in the parks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the hotel shuttle or a short rideshare to Disney Springs — Disney's free-admission shopping, dining, and entertainment district. Explore the four neighborhoods: The Landing, Marketplace, Town Center, and West Side. Visit the LEGO Store (free to browse), World of Disney (largest Disney merchandise store), and enjoy free street entertainment. Browse the unique shops and enjoy the waterfront atmosphere. Visit the free Splitsville Luxury Lanes exterior area and enjoy the lively atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Use your park ticket for a late-afternoon/evening entry to Magic Kingdom (if using a multi-day ticket with park hopper, or save this as your Magic Kingdom day). Arrive around 4:00-5:00 PM when morning crowds have thinned. Ride any attractions you missed on Day 2, catch the evening parade, and stay for the fireworks. Alternatively, enjoy a relaxed dinner at Disney Springs and explore the free entertainment before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Cook simple breakfast items purchased from Publix in the hotel room (if kitchenette available) or grab a continental breakfast at the hotel. Budget: ~$3-6 per person.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch with groceries from Publix — sandwiches, fruit, chips, and drinks eaten at the hotel or a park bench at Disney Springs (~$5-8 per person). Huge savings!
meals.dinner: At Disney Springs: Earl of Sandwich — one of the best budget dining options near Disney with hot sandwiches, salads, and soups at very reasonable prices (~$10-13 per person). Or try Chicken Guy! by Guy Fieri for affordable chicken tenders and sandwiches (~$12-15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Disney Springs is completely FREE to enter — no park ticket required! Parking is also free (if driving). This is a great budget day to rest your feet while still enjoying Disney magic. The free entertainment, beautiful waterfront setting, and unique shops make it a worthwhile half-day. If you have a Park Hopper ticket, use the evening for a second visit to your favorite park.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of the hotel (or store luggage at the front desk if flight is later). If time permits before departure, take one final trip to your favorite Disney park for a few last rides, or explore the Kissimmee/Orlando area near the hotel. International Drive (I-Drive) is about 15 minutes away and offers free/cheap attractions like the Orlando International Premium Outlets for souvenir shopping at discounted prices. Alternatively, visit Old Town Kissimmee (free admission) on W Irlo Bronson Hwy — a retro-themed shopping and entertainment complex just minutes from the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, head to Orlando International Airport. Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for check-in, security, and boarding. Take a rideshare (Lyft/Uber ~$25-35) or arrange a hotel shuttle to the airport. Browse the airport shops for any last-minute souvenirs — Orlando airport has good options at reasonable prices compared to the parks.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Orlando with incredible memories! Review your photos and videos from the trip. If your flight is delayed or you have extra time, the airport has several dining options at various price points.

meals.breakfast: Use up remaining groceries from Publix for a hotel room breakfast before checkout (~$3-5 per person). Or grab a quick breakfast at McDonald's or Dunkin' on W Irlo Bronson Hwy (~$5-8 per person).
meals.lunch: If visiting Old Town or I-Drive: grab a quick and affordable meal at one of the many fast-casual restaurants in the area. Subway, Chipotle, or local spots offer good value (~$8-12 per person). At the airport: grab food before security if possible as it's cheaper than post-security options.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the plane. Budget ~$15-20 per person for airport food if needed.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — ask the hotel to store your luggage if your flight is in the afternoon. Return any rented items and double-check your room for forgotten belongings. The hotel's free theme park shuttle may not run to the airport — confirm transportation options at check-in. Keep receipts for any travel insurance claims. Total estimated food budget for the week (excluding park meals): $40-60 per person by using grocery store snacks and strategic counter-service dining.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 22:30. Take ground transportation or a rideshare to Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway. Check in, unpack, and settle into your room. Pick up any essentials at a nearby 24-hour Walmart or Walgreens on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In transit
meals.lunch: N/A – In transit
meals.dinner: Late-night snack or quick bite at a nearby fast-food option such as McDonald's or Denny's on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy (open 24 hours), both within 1–2 miles of the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – rest is essential after a late arrival. Confirm your hotel shuttle schedule for the next morning and download the My Disney Experience app if you haven't already. Pre-purchase park tickets and make Lightning Lane reservations in advance to save time.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Park Full Day – Begin with an early morning arrival via the hotel's free theme park shuttle (aim for the first shuttle, typically around 8:00 AM). Enter Magic Kingdom at rope drop and head straight to Tomorrowland for Space Mountain before crowds build. Follow up with The Haunted Mansion and Pirates of the Caribbean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Magic Kingdom. Ride Big Thunder Mountain Railroad and Seven Dwarfs Mine Train using Lightning Lane reservations. Explore Fantasyland with younger family members. Take a midday break in the shade at Storybook Treats or find a bench near the castle to recharge.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the evening spectacular – watch the Magic Kingdom fireworks show 'Disney Enchantment' (typically at 9:00 PM in summer). Grab a prime viewing spot on Main Street U.S.A. about 30 minutes before showtime. Return to hotel via the free shuttle after the show.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast at the hotel or pick up pastries and coffee at Main Street Bakery inside Magic Kingdom (Casey's Corner area) – budget around $10–$15 per person.
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square – a mid-range counter-service spot offering clam chowder, lobster rolls, and fried fish. Budget around $15–$20 per person.
meals.dinner: The Plaza Restaurant on Main Street U.S.A. – a table-service option with classic American sandwiches and entrées. Budget around $20–$35 per person. Make an advance dining reservation via My Disney Experience.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable, breathable clothing as June in Orlando is hot and humid (expect 90°F+). Bring sunscreen, a refillable water bottle, and a small poncho for afternoon thunderstorms. The free hotel shuttle typically runs every 30–60 minutes – confirm the last shuttle time at check-in.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour – Take the hotel shuttle to EPCOT. Arrive at opening and head to Future World (now called World Discovery and World Nature) to ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind and Test Track early before lines grow. Use Lightning Lane for Frozen Ever After.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transition to the World Showcase Lagoon and begin your food and culture tour. Stroll through the 11 country pavilions – Mexico, Norway, China, Germany, Italy, America, Japan, Morocco, France, United Kingdom, and Canada. Sample small bites and drinks from 3–4 pavilions. Don't miss the Mexico pavilion's Gran Fiesta Tour boat ride.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for EPCOT's 'EPCOT Forever' or 'Harmonious' nighttime spectacular over World Showcase Lagoon (check current show schedule on the My Disney Experience app). Watch from the World Showcase promenade for the best views. Return to hotel via shuttle.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at the hotel continental breakfast or stop at Sunshine Seasons in EPCOT's Land Pavilion – a great counter-service option with fresh, healthy choices. Budget $10–$15 per person.
meals.lunch: World Showcase food stalls – graze through 2–3 countries. Try a crepe from France, a bratwurst from Germany, and a taco from Mexico. Budget $20–$30 per person for a satisfying spread.
meals.dinner: Teppan Edo in the Japan Pavilion – a fun, interactive teppanyaki table-service experience perfect for families. Budget $30–$45 per person. Book an advance dining reservation.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is a large park – wear comfortable walking shoes. The World Showcase doesn't open until 11:00 AM, so use the morning for Future World attractions. Check the My Disney Experience app for live entertainment schedules in each pavilion – cultural performances are free and entertaining.

day_by_day.morning: Hollywood Studios Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Adventure – Take the hotel shuttle to Hollywood Studios. Arrive at rope drop and head directly to Galaxy's Edge (Star Wars land). Join the virtual queue or Lightning Lane for Rise of the Resistance – one of Disney's most immersive rides. Then visit Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Savi's Workshop to build a custom lightsaber (approximately $249.99 per lightsaber – optional splurge, book in advance). Alternatively, browse Dok-Ondar's Den of Antiquities for Star Wars collectibles. Then head to Toy Story Land for Slinky Dog Dash and Toy Story Mania. Catch a showing of Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the 'Fantasmic!' nighttime show at the Hollywood Hills Amphitheater (check current schedule). Arrive 45–60 minutes early for good seating. After the show, take the hotel shuttle back to Kissimmee.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the hotel or pick up a quick bite at Ronto Roasters in Galaxy's Edge – try the Ronto Morning Wrap (a fan favorite). Budget $12–$15 per person.
meals.lunch: Docking Bay 7 Food and Cargo in Galaxy's Edge – a themed counter-service restaurant with creative dishes like Smoked Kaadu Ribs and Fried Endorian Tip-Yip. Budget $15–$22 per person.
meals.dinner: 50's Prime Time Café in Hollywood Studios – a nostalgic, fun table-service restaurant with classic American comfort food served in a 1950s TV-show setting. Budget $20–$35 per person. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Galaxy's Edge is extremely popular – arrive early and use Lightning Lane reservations for Rise of the Resistance. If building a lightsaber at Savi's Workshop, book the reservation weeks in advance as slots fill up fast. Lightsaber building is a memorable but pricey experience – factor it into your budget separately.

day_by_day.morning: Animal Kingdom – Kilimanjaro Safari & Avatar Flight of Passage – Take the hotel shuttle to Animal Kingdom. Arrive at rope drop and head immediately to Pandora – The World of Avatar for Flight of Passage (one of Disney's most popular rides). Use Lightning Lane if available. Follow up with Na'vi River Journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Africa for the Kilimanjaro Safari – book an early afternoon time slot for the best animal activity. Spot lions, elephants, giraffes, rhinos, and more in a realistic savanna setting. Explore the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail on foot afterward. Visit Asia for Expedition Everest and Kali River Rapids (bring a change of clothes or a poncho).
day_by_day.evening: Catch the 'Rivers of Light' or 'Tree of Life Awakenings' evening experience (check current schedule). The Tree of Life comes alive with projected animal imagery after dark – a magical, free experience. Return to hotel via shuttle.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a quick snack at Harambe Market near the Africa section of Animal Kingdom – try the Kenyan coffee and a pastry. Budget $10–$14 per person.
meals.lunch: Satu'li Canteen in Pandora – a popular counter-service spot with healthy, flavorful bowls and unique Pandora-themed dishes. Budget $15–$20 per person.
meals.dinner: Yak & Yeti Restaurant in Asia – a table-service restaurant with Asian-fusion cuisine including Mandarin chicken, dim sum, and ahi tuna. Budget $20–$35 per person. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom closes earlier than other parks (typically 8:00–9:00 PM in summer). Plan your day accordingly. Kali River Rapids will get you wet – bring a change of clothes or a waterproof bag for valuables. June heat makes the shaded jungle trails in Animal Kingdom a welcome relief.

day_by_day.morning: Disney Springs Family Entertainment Day – Take the hotel shuttle to Disney Springs (free admission, no park ticket required). Arrive mid-morning and explore the shopping, entertainment, and street performances. Visit the LEGO Store, World of Disney (the largest Disney merchandise store), and browse the unique boutiques in the Town Center area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy free street entertainment and live music performances throughout Disney Springs. Visit Splitsville Luxury Lanes for bowling (budget activity, approximately $15–$20 per person per game). Alternatively, check out the AMC Disney Springs 24 movie theater for a matinee showing. Let kids explore the interactive water features and splash zones near the Marketplace area.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed dinner at Disney Springs before heading back to the hotel. Spend the evening at the hotel pool to rest tired feet before your final park day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the hotel or stop at Amorette's Patisserie at Disney Springs for fresh pastries and coffee. Budget $10–$15 per person.
meals.lunch: D-Luxe Burger at Disney Springs – a mid-range counter-service spot with gourmet burgers, hand-cut fries, and milkshakes. Budget $15–$20 per person.
meals.dinner: The Boathouse at Disney Springs – a waterfront table-service restaurant with fresh seafood, steaks, and classic American dishes. Budget $30–$50 per person. A slightly elevated mid-range splurge for a special evening. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Disney Springs is free to enter and a great budget-friendly day compared to the theme parks. Parking is also free. The hotel shuttle may or may not service Disney Springs directly – confirm with the front desk. If not, a rideshare from Kissimmee to Disney Springs is approximately $10–$15 each way. This is a great rest day to recharge before the final park day.

day_by_day.morning: Return to a Favorite Park or Revisit Highlights – Based on your family's favorites from the week, choose one park to revisit for a final morning. Magic Kingdom is recommended for a nostalgic farewell. Arrive at rope drop via the hotel shuttle and tackle any rides you missed or want to experience again. Use remaining Lightning Lane passes wisely.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the early afternoon wrapping up your park visit. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs from the park gift shops or World of Disney at Disney Springs. Head back to the hotel by 3:00–4:00 PM to pack, check out, and prepare for departure. Store luggage with the hotel concierge if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Depart for Orlando International Airport or continue to your next destination. If your flight is late evening, enjoy a farewell dinner near the hotel in Kissimmee before heading to the airport.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast at the hotel or pick up pastries and coffee at the park upon arrival. Budget $10–$15 per person.
meals.lunch: Enjoy one final themed lunch inside your chosen park. Casey's Corner at Magic Kingdom (hot dogs and corn dog nuggets) is a fun, affordable counter-service option. Budget $12–$18 per person.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner near the hotel – Perkins Restaurant & Bakery on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy is a family-friendly, mid-range option with hearty American comfort food. Budget $15–$25 per person. Alternatively, try Azteca's Mexican Restaurant nearby for a casual, affordable meal.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport travel and security. Orlando International Airport is approximately 25–30 minutes from the Kissimmee hotel without traffic, but June summer traffic can add time. Book a rideshare or taxi in advance. Double-check all hotel charges, return any rental items, and confirm shuttle or transport arrangements the night before departure.

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway - Free Theme Park Shuttle
hotel.location: 7470 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, US (28.3314,-81.5863)

experiences.name: Magic Kingdom Park Full Day
experiences.description: Experience the iconic Magic Kingdom with classic rides like Space Mountain, Pirates of the Caribbean, and the Haunted Mansion. Watch the Festival of Fantasy parade and end the night with the spectacular Happily Ever After fireworks show over Cinderella Castle.
experiences.location: Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

experiences.name: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour
experiences.description: Explore 11 country pavilions around World Showcase Lagoon, sampling authentic cuisines from Mexico, Japan, France, Morocco, and more. Enjoy live cultural performances, artisan demonstrations, and the stunning EPCOT Forever nighttime spectacular over the lagoon.
experiences.location: EPCOT World Showcase, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

experiences.name: Hollywood Studios Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Adventure
experiences.description: Immerse your family in the Star Wars universe at Batuu. Build a custom lightsaber at Savi's Workshop, pilot the Millennium Falcon on Smugglers Run, and experience the thrilling Rise of the Resistance ride. Dine at the Oga's Cantina for themed drinks and snacks.
experiences.location: Hollywood Studios, Galaxy's Edge, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

experiences.name: Disney Springs Family Entertainment Day
experiences.description: Spend a budget-friendly day at Disney Springs exploring free entertainment, street performers, and unique dining. Visit the LEGO Store, enjoy a meal at T-REX Cafe, catch a movie at the AMC Disney Springs 24, and browse over 100 shops and restaurants with no park admission required.
experiences.location: Disney Springs, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

experiences.name: Animal Kingdom Kilimanjaro Safari & Avatar Flight of Passage
experiences.description: Start your morning with a Kilimanjaro Safari to spot lions, elephants, giraffes, and rhinos in a realistic savanna setting. Then soar over Pandora on the breathtaking Avatar Flight of Passage ride. Explore the Pandora World of Avatar at dusk when the bioluminescent landscape glows beautifully.
experiences.location: Animal Kingdom, Pandora & Africa Sections, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight UA arrives at 22:30. No morning or afternoon activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit. Flight arrives late evening.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 22:30. Use Ramada's complimentary theme park shuttle or arrange a private car transfer to the hotel. Check in to Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway. Unwind with a late-night snack from the hotel's amenities or a nearby 24-hour convenience stop.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night arrival – grab a light bite at the hotel or a nearby late-night spot such as Denny's (open 24 hrs, 2 min drive) or order room service if available

day_by_day.notes: Pack light carry-on essentials for easy late-night check-in. Confirm shuttle schedule with the hotel in advance or pre-book a private luxury car service (e.g., Mears Connect Black Car) for a seamless arrival. Get to bed early – big park days start tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Park Full Day – Arrive at rope drop (park opens ~9:00 AM). Use the hotel's free theme park shuttle (departs ~8:00 AM). Hit the top-tier attractions first: Space Mountain, Seven Dwarfs Mine Train (book Lightning Lane Multi Pass in advance), and Pirates of the Caribbean. Explore Fantasyland and Tomorrowland before crowds build.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Magic Kingdom exploration. Experience Haunted Mansion, Big Thunder Mountain Railroad, and the iconic Jungle Cruise. Take a midday break at a shaded area or a sit-down restaurant to recharge during peak afternoon heat. Use Lightning Lane Individual selections for Seven Dwarfs Mine Train if not done in the morning.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the spectacular Magic Kingdom nighttime shows: Disney Enchantment fireworks spectacular and the Main Street Electrical Parade (check current schedule). Enjoy the magical atmosphere of Main Street U.S.A. lit up at night before taking the shuttle back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before shuttle departure – or grab a quick bite at Magic Kingdom's Main Street Bakery (Starbucks partner) upon arrival
meals.lunch: Be Our Guest Restaurant (Beauty and the Beast themed, table service) – reserve well in advance via My Disney Experience app. Enjoy French-inspired cuisine in the Beast's enchanted castle
meals.dinner: Cinderella's Royal Table inside Cinderella Castle – a premium character dining experience with prix-fixe menu featuring roasted beef tenderloin, pan-seared salmon, and decadent desserts. Book 60 days in advance

day_by_day.notes: Download the My Disney Experience app and pre-purchase Lightning Lane Multi Pass ($25–$35/person/day) before arrival. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sunscreen, a portable fan, and a refillable water bottle. Magic Kingdom is the most popular park – arriving at rope drop is essential for a premium experience.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour – Take the hotel shuttle to EPCOT (opens ~9:00 AM). Begin in Future World/World Discovery: experience Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (book Individual Lightning Lane at 7:00 AM sharp), Test Track, and Soarin' Around the World. These are best tackled early before lines grow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transition to the World Showcase Lagoon (opens 11:00 AM). Embark on a self-guided food and culture tour through all 11 country pavilions – Mexico, Norway, China, Germany, Italy, America, Japan, Morocco, France, United Kingdom, and Canada. Sample signature dishes and beverages at each pavilion. Highlights: Remy's Ratatouille Adventure in France Pavilion (Lightning Lane recommended), frozen margaritas in Mexico, and Kringla Bakeri in Norway.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy EPCOT's stunning EPCOT Forever or Harmonious nighttime spectacular over World Showcase Lagoon (check current show schedule). Browse unique international merchandise and artisan shops. Take the shuttle back to the hotel after the show.

meals.breakfast: The Garden Grill Restaurant at EPCOT (The Land Pavilion) – rotating character breakfast with Chip 'n' Dale, Mickey, and Pluto. Farm-fresh American cuisine in a slowly rotating dining room overlooking Living with the Land boat ride
meals.lunch: World Showcase food crawl – graze through multiple pavilions. Must-tries: School Bread (Norway), Beef Gyoza (Japan), Crêpes (France), and Lobster Bisque (Canada). Budget ~$15–$25 per stop
meals.dinner: Monsieur Paul – EPCOT's most upscale dining experience in the France Pavilion. Classic French haute cuisine with dishes like duck foie gras, pan-seared scallops, and Grand Marnier soufflé. Stunning lagoon views. Reserve 60 days ahead

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is the largest Disney park – wear very comfortable shoes. The World Showcase food tour is a highlight for foodies and families alike. Consider purchasing the EPCOT International Food & Wine Festival add-ons if visiting during that season (typically August–November). Stay hydrated – June heat in Orlando can reach 90°F+ with high humidity.

day_by_day.morning: Hollywood Studios – Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Adventure. Take the early shuttle to Hollywood Studios (opens ~9:00 AM). Head directly to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge at Batuu. First priority: book a time slot for Savi's Workshop – Handbuilt Lightsabers ($249.99/person, ~45 min experience) – this must be reserved in advance via My Disney Experience. Also experience Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run (Lightning Lane recommended).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Star Wars experience with Rise of the Resistance (one of Disney's most immersive rides – book Individual Lightning Lane at 7:00 AM). Visit Droid Depot to build a custom astromech droid ($119.99). Explore the rest of Hollywood Studios: Toy Story Land (Slinky Dog Dash), Tower of Terror, and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster Starring Aerosmith.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the breathtaking Fantasmic! nighttime show at the Hollywood Hills Amphitheater (check schedule – typically 8:00 PM and 10:00 PM). Arrive 45–60 minutes early for good seats, or book the Fantasmic! Dining Package for reserved seating. End the night with a stroll through the beautifully lit Hollywood Boulevard before shuttling back.

meals.breakfast: Grab-and-go from hotel or quick service at Hollywood Studios' Trolley Car Café (Starbucks) upon arrival
meals.lunch: Sci-Fi Dine-In Theater Restaurant – a unique table-service experience where you dine in vintage cars under a simulated starry night sky watching classic sci-fi movie clips. American comfort food with burgers, milkshakes, and sandwiches
meals.dinner: Fantasmic! Dining Package at Hollywood & Vine – buffet-style dinner with character meet-and-greets (Disney Junior characters) plus guaranteed reserved Fantasmic! seating. Alternatively, The Hollywood Brown Derby for upscale California cuisine and the famous Cobb Salad

day_by_day.notes: Savi's Workshop and Droid Depot reservations are extremely limited and sell out weeks in advance – book immediately upon planning. The lightsaber building experience is a premium highlight and worth every penny for Star Wars fans. Bring a tote bag for your lightsaber and droid. Rise of the Resistance is a 15-minute immersive experience unlike anything else at Disney.

day_by_day.morning: Animal Kingdom – Kilimanjaro Safari & Avatar Flight of Passage. Take the early shuttle to Animal Kingdom (opens ~8:00 AM – often has early entry). Head immediately to Pandora – The World of Avatar for Avatar: Flight of Passage (the park's most popular ride – book Individual Lightning Lane at 7:00 AM or arrive at rope drop). The Na'vi River Journey is a beautiful, immersive boat ride perfect for all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kilimanjaro Safari (best in morning or late afternoon for active animals – book a second ride if possible). Spot lions, elephants, giraffes, rhinos, hippos, and more in a realistic savanna setting. Explore Africa and Asia sections: Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail, Maharajah Jungle Trek, and DINOSAUR attraction. Enjoy the Festival of the Lion King live show (check schedule).
day_by_day.evening: Experience the Tree of Life Awakenings – a stunning projection show on the iconic Tree of Life after dark (check schedule). Rivers of Light nighttime spectacular if available. Enjoy the magical atmosphere of Animal Kingdom at dusk before heading back to the hotel for a relaxing evening.

meals.breakfast: Tusker House Restaurant – Donald Duck's Safari Breakfast character dining experience with African-inspired buffet including carved meats, bobotie, and fresh pastries. A premium character dining experience in a beautiful setting
meals.lunch: Satu'li Canteen in Pandora – The World of Avatar. Healthy, flavorful bowls with proteins like slow-roasted Rongi beans, chili-spiced crispy chicken, and wood-grilled beef. Stunning bioluminescent décor
meals.dinner: Jiko – The Cooking Place at Disney's Animal Kingdom Lodge (short Uber/Lyft ride from the park, ~10 min). One of Walt Disney World's finest restaurants featuring African-inspired cuisine: oak-grilled filet mignon, Durban-spiced chicken, and an award-winning South African wine list. Stunning savanna views

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom is the most nature-focused Disney park – it's genuinely beautiful and worth taking time to appreciate the landscaping and animal habitats. The park closes earlier than others (typically 8–9 PM). Consider booking a Wild Africa Trek ($189–$249/person) for a behind-the-scenes guided safari experience – book well in advance. Bring insect repellent for the outdoor trails.

day_by_day.morning: Disney Springs Family Entertainment Day – Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely morning. Take a late shuttle or Uber to Disney Springs (free admission, no park ticket required). Explore the 4 neighborhoods: The Landing, Marketplace, Town Center, and West Side. Browse world-class shopping including LEGO Store, World of Disney (largest Disney merchandise store), and unique boutiques. Visit the Marketplace Co-Op for artisan Disney goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy Disney Springs' free entertainment: live street performers, musicians, and interactive experiences. Visit Splitsville Luxury Lanes for premium bowling and entertainment ($18–$25/person). Explore the AMC Disney Springs 24 for a movie if desired. Browse the Art of Disney gallery. Kids can enjoy the interactive water features and splash pads in the Marketplace area.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed, premium evening at Disney Springs. Explore the vibrant nightlife atmosphere with live music at various venues. Return to the hotel for a relaxing evening – consider booking an in-room spa treatment or using hotel pool facilities. Pack bags for checkout if departing soon.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast or brunch – sleep in and enjoy a relaxed start
meals.lunch: The BOATHOUSE – Disney Springs' premier waterfront dining experience. Upscale American seafood and steakhouse with stunning marina views. Signature dishes: whole Maine lobster, dry-aged prime steaks, and fresh oysters. Amphibicar tours available from the dock
meals.dinner: Morimoto Asia – Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto's flagship Asian restaurant at Disney Springs. Pan-Asian cuisine featuring Peking duck, dim sum, sushi, and signature cocktails in a stunning two-story space. One of the best restaurants in all of Orlando

day_by_day.notes: Disney Springs is free to enter and a great way to experience Disney magic without a park ticket. Saturday is typically the busiest day – arrive at Disney Springs by 10:00 AM to beat crowds. The BOATHOUSE and Morimoto Asia are extremely popular – reservations are essential (book via OpenTable or Disney's dining reservation system 60 days ahead). This is a great recovery day after four intense park days.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning – Return to a favorite park or explore a missed experience. Recommended: revisit EPCOT or Magic Kingdom for any missed attractions. Alternatively, enjoy a premium resort experience: book a morning spa treatment at a nearby luxury spa (Senses Spa at Disney's Grand Floridian, ~15 min Uber), or enjoy a leisurely pool morning at the hotel. For families, consider a character breakfast at one of the Disney resort hotels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping and final Disney experiences. Visit the World of Disney store at Disney Springs for last-minute gifts. Pack and prepare for departure. Check out of Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway. Store luggage with the front desk if needed for a late departure.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Orlando International Airport. Arrange private car service or use hotel shuttle (confirm schedule with front desk). Arrive at the airport 2.5–3 hours before international/domestic departure. Reflect on an incredible week of Disney magic!

meals.breakfast: Chef Mickey's at Disney's Contemporary Resort (short Uber ride) – the ultimate Disney character breakfast with Mickey, Minnie, Donald, Goofy, and Pluto. American breakfast buffet in a stunning monorail-level dining room. A perfect final Disney memory
meals.lunch: California Grill at Disney's Contemporary Resort (same location as breakfast or return trip) – upscale California cuisine with panoramic views of Magic Kingdom. Sushi, wood-fired flatbreads, and farm-to-table entrées. Request a window table for Magic Kingdom views
meals.dinner: Airport dining or an early dinner near the hotel before departure – consider Charley's Steak House & Market Fresh Fish (5 min from hotel) for a premium farewell steak dinner, or grab a final meal at Disney Springs if time permits

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM – request a late checkout (1:00–2:00 PM) in advance if your flight departs in the evening. Orlando International Airport (MCO) is approximately 25–30 minutes from the hotel without traffic, but allow extra time on weekends. Consider enrolling in Disney's Magical Express or using Mears Connect for a seamless airport transfer. Download all your Disney PhotoPass photos before leaving – purchase Memory Maker ($169) for unlimited digital downloads of all ride photos and character meet photos taken throughout the trip.

query: Disney World Orlando family of 4, $6000, 7 days, June
